articles.title: Google Hotels Printed $17 for a Stay It Itemised at $16.66
articles.excerpt: I run a visa agency in Bali. The other half of my week goes into scrapers on Apify, and one of them reads Google Hotels: a place and two dates in, one row per property out. A row carries four price nu…
articles.body: I run a visa agency in Bali. The other half of my week goes into scrapers on Apify, and one of them reads Google Hotels: a place and two dates in, one row per property out. A row carries four price numbers for the stay. totalPrice , priceBeforeTaxes , taxesAndFees , totalWithTaxes . Google labels none of them, because Google doesn't ship them as named fields — they come out of an unnamed array, and what each slot means is something you work out or guess. I guessed. My own README said totalPrice includes taxes and fees. Then a $17 homestay made me go and count.
articles.author: Matvey

So instead of only reading about LLMs, I decided to build a small language model from scratch using PyTorch . The goal wasn't to build the next ChatGPT. The goal was much more important for me as a learner: What I Built The model starts with Shakespeare text and learns to predict the next character.

articles.title: When a Customer Switches Plans Mid-Month and You Have Under 50 Subscribers
articles.excerpt: Say a customer on your $19/month Starter plan emails on the 16th: "can I move to Pro today? I need the export thing." You open Stripe, swap the price on their subscription, and reply "done". What did…
articles.body: Say a customer on your $19/month Starter plan emails on the 16th: "can I move to Pro today? I need the export thing." You open Stripe, swap the price on their subscription, and reply "done". What did they just pay? Nothing yet, most likely. And on the 1st they'll get an invoice for $64 instead of $49, and you'll get an email asking why. That's proration. It's not a bug, it's Stripe doing exactly what the default says. But when you have under 50 subscribers, every one of these plan changes is a support thread with your name on it, so it's worth knowing what each switch actually charges before you click. This is the version I'd want: upgrades, downgrades, monthly to annual, the four traps, and how to check the number before the customer sees it. Not tax or accounting advice.

articles.title: I Built a Life Simulator That Deals You a Random Country at Birth — With Real UN Data
articles.excerpt: Every life simulator starts the same way: you design your character. Pick a country, pick a family, optimize the stats. I wanted the opposite. Real life doesn't let you pick — you are dealt a country,…
articles.body: Every life simulator starts the same way: you design your character. Pick a country, pick a family, optimize the stats. I wanted the opposite. Real life doesn't let you pick — you are dealt a country, a family, a body, at random, weighted by how many babies are actually born in each place. So I built a game around the deal itself: 1in8b.dev — "1 in 8 billion". You press one button, and you are born somewhere on Earth, with probabilities proportional to real birth counts. Then you live that life, year by year, until the local statistics say you don't.

articles.title: How to Tell if a CBE or Telebirr Payment Screenshot Is Fake
articles.excerpt: Type "fake cbe" into Google and autocomplete offers "fake cbe screenshot template" and "fake cbe app". Type "fake telebirr" and it offers "fake telebirr app for android". That's what you're up against…
articles.body: Type "fake cbe" into Google and autocomplete offers "fake cbe screenshot template" and "fake cbe app". Type "fake telebirr" and it offers "fake telebirr app for android". That's what you're up against at the counter: tools made to draw a convincing success screen without any money moving. I maintain cheki.et , a free, open-source checker for Ethiopian bank and wallet receipts, so I spend a lot of time looking at real and fake ones. The short version of everything below: a screenshot can't prove a payment. Only the bank's record can. The rest is about getting to that record quickly while a customer waits. What a fake usually is Most fake "payments" fall into five kinds: An edited real receipt. A genuine 500 birr transfer becomes 5,000 birr, or an old date becomes today.
articles.author: Ray

articles.title: Verify CBE and Telebirr payments in your app with a free API
articles.excerpt: If you sell anything online in Ethiopia, you know the flow: the customer pays by bank transfer or Telebirr, then sends a screenshot. Someone on your team looks at it and decides whether to ship. Scree…
articles.body: If you sell anything online in Ethiopia, you know the flow: the customer pays by bank transfer or Telebirr, then sends a screenshot. Someone on your team looks at it and decides whether to ship. Screenshots are easy to edit and easy to reuse, so that decision is a guess. I maintain cheki.et , a free, MIT-licensed receipt checker, and this post is the developer version: how to confirm a payment against the bank's own record from your backend, in a few lines of Node or Python. One thing first, because it's the most common confusion I see. Searching "telebirr api" or "cbe api" mostly turns up payment collection : merchant APIs where you start a payment and get a callback. Those need a merchant agreement with the bank. What I'm describing is the other half.
articles.author: Ray

Teams deploy autonomous agents to build features, fix bugs, run test suites, and execute deployments. However, operating multiple agent sessions in the same terminal environment quickly exposes three critical concurrency and governance hazards: Race Conditions & Write Collisions: When two agent sessions attempt to run git commands, build artifacts, or modify configuration files simultaneously, uncoordinated processes overwrite each other, producing corrupt states or broken builds.

articles.title: Cooking Up Magick Book Review
articles.excerpt: Cooking Up Magick Book Review
articles.body: The first book in a new series called The Dell Chronicles, HL Bernabe’s Cooking Up Magick sets out to be a cozier fantasy version of The Lord of the Rings . And in many ways, it does pull directly from J.R.R. Tolkien’s world. The main character, Paisley, is a halfling who gets swept up on an adventure with a pair of dwarves, but unbeknownst to her, there’s also an evil overlord that has just returned after centuries – and she’s the only hope the world has to actually stop him. The similarities to The Hobbit and LOTR pretty much end there though, and you don’t get nearly enough detail in the first book to effectively flesh out this alternate version of Middle-earth. What you do get is a lovable main character who is surrounded by an interesting cast of characters.
